title: Planning an industrial skid package procurement
summary: A procurement checklist for skid-mounted process equipment, including battery limits, utilities, controls, certification, transport and site interfaces.
body:
A modular skid can combine vessels, heat-transfer equipment, pumps, piping, valves, instruments and controls into a package assembled and tested before shipment. To compare offers fairly, the buyer and supplier should agree on the package boundaries and interfaces at the start.

1. Define the process duty and battery limits

Share the process description, available PFD or P&ID, flow rates, fluid composition, operating and design conditions, capacity targets and expected operating modes. Define what is inside the supplier's scope and what will be provided by the EPC contractor or site team. Battery limits should identify the process tie-ins, utility connections, electrical supply and control-system interfaces.

2. Make the equipment and control scope explicit

Confirm the equipment list and identify whether the package includes vessels, heat exchangers, pumps, filters, valves, instruments, local panels, control cabinets, piping, supports and access platforms. State the required control philosophy, signal interfaces, communication protocols and any hazardous-area requirements. Avoid assuming that all auxiliaries or site cabling are included unless they are listed in the scope.

3. Align codes, inspection and documents

List the applicable mechanical and piping codes, material requirements, inspection and testing plan, pressure tests, examination requirements, certificates and documentation language. If regional conformity assessment or third-party inspection is required, specify it early because it may affect the schedule, documentation and cost.

4. Check transport and site installation constraints

Provide the destination, maximum transport envelope, lifting restrictions, route constraints where known and available installation space. Confirm whether the skid will be shipped fully assembled or in modules. Define who is responsible for unloading, foundations, interconnecting piping, field wiring, insulation, commissioning and performance testing.

5. Compare quotations on the same basis

  • Same process design basis and equipment quantity.
  • Same battery limits, accessories, instruments and control scope.
  • Same code, inspection, certification and documentation requirements.
  • Same delivery term, packing, transport assumptions and schedule basis.
  • Clear exclusions, client-supplied items and site-work responsibilities.

When is a budgetary offer appropriate?

A budgetary offer can help establish project feasibility when some details are still under development. The offer should identify assumptions, exclusions and information still required. Final technical and commercial terms should be based on an agreed scope and reviewed project documents.

For an initial scope review, share the available PFD, P&ID, equipment list and site constraints through our project inquiry page.
